clue.text: Lusts wickedly and earl creates conflict

indicators.note: behaving wickedly suggests the letters of the word before are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A lustful aristocrat's misconduct sparks a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wickedly' turns LUSTS into TUSSL; E for earl finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuffle or struggle is a form of conflict, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Tenor performed hip hop in a tight corner

parts.note: to rap is to perform hip hop vocals

explanation.surface: A tenor tried rapping and found himself in difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught with no way out is the idiomatic sense of a tight corner.

clue.text: Stay beside the sea

definitions.meaning: a prop or support; to stay a wall is to prop it
the land along the edge of the sea

explanation.surface: An invitation to remain at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up with a timber is to support, the sense of stay; the coast is the land beside the sea.

clue.text: Inspect small instrument and be quick about it

parts.note: to look at something is to inspect it
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Examine a little instrument, and hurry up about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom urging haste: move briskly, get a move on.

clue.text: Scruffy punk met disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so the letters of the two words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A punk rocker had a bad encounter and came away looking dishevelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' scrambles PUNK MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe an untidy, uncared-for appearance; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Anxious when riding neck and neck

parts.note: a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up
a tight race is one that is neck and neck

explanation.surface: A jockey is nervous in a close finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing a jockey 'up' is riding the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense and nervous, an informal synonym for anxious.

clue.text: Poet and knight feast on Sunday

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for knight in chess notation
to feast on is to eat

explanation.surface: A poet and a knight dine richly on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Horse carries mother and boy in preserve

indicators.note: carries means the horse word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
MA is a familiar word for mother
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A horse bears a mother and son into a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserve' looks like a verb but is the noun, a fruit spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit preserve or conserve made from citrus, usually oranges.

clue.text: Nurse turned up coloured fabric

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the phrase is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: red is a colour
net is an open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A nurse has turned up wearing coloured cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the whole of RED NET, giving TENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who looks after or tends someone is a carer; a nurse tends patients.

clue.text: Woman is cruel after losing bridge partner

indicators.note: losing means the letter for a bridge partner drops out of the cruel word

parts.note: violent means brutal or cruel
in bridge North and South are partners, so N is a bridge partner

explanation.surface: A woman turns nasty after her bridge partner lets her down.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North partners South, so either letter can be a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Violet is a female first name, an example of a woman in crosswords.

clue.text: Defender gets a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist of something is its main point

explanation.surface: A sports defender scores a point in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defender' suggests a sports position, but it means someone who argues in support of a cause.
explanation.definitionFit: One who speaks or writes in defence of a belief or cause is its advocate or champion.

clue.text: Artist returned and administered the island

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation for artist is read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to run a business is to administer it

explanation.surface: A painter came back and governed an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns RA into AR. Arran is an island off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is a Scottish island in the Firth of Clyde, a specific example of an island.

clue.text: Shanghai journalists?

definitions.meaning: to shanghai someone is to force them into service
the body of newspaper reporters collectively

explanation.surface: A question about reporters working in the Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: Shanghai looks like the city, but here it is a verb: to kidnap a man into a ship's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress sailors is to force them into service; reporters as a group are known as the fourth estate.

clue.text: Member is slow to pass laws

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
late here means behind time, slow to arrive

explanation.surface: A parliamentary member is sluggish in getting laws through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests an MP, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Making statutes by enacting them is exactly what a parliament does when it creates law.

clue.text: Belittle Germany and Spain with monograph

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet on one subject

explanation.surface: Germany and Spain issue a pamphlet disparaging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish or take away from something's worth is to disparage it; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Walk round stable that's highly thought of

indicators.note: round means the walking word goes around the stable word

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure means steady or stable

explanation.surface: Taking a walk round a well-regarded stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like a noun for horses but is the adjective, SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cherished or valued greatly is highly prized, highly thought of.

clue.text: Danger for doctor taking heroin

indicators.note: taking means the doctoring word takes the drug's letter inside it

parts.note: to doctor a patient is to treat them
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A doctor using heroin poses a danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb here, giving TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace or source of possible harm is a danger; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Carnivore died in butt of port

indicators.note: in means the carnivore and died letters sit inside the butting word

parts.note: to butt is to ram
the otter is a meat-eating mammal

explanation.surface: A carnivore died in a cask at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a barrel but is the verb, RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major Dutch seaport, an example of a port.

clue.text: Mind about record being promoted

indicators.note: about means the word for mind goes round the record

parts.note: to mind is to heed, take notice of
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: Care is needed when a record is being plugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mind' is a verb, HEED, placed about LP.
explanation.definitionFit: To promote a cause is to further or assist it, so the past forms share a meaning.

clue.text: Flower not properly ripened

indicators.note: not properly means the letters of ripened are arranged wrongly

explanation.surface: A bloom that has not quite matured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a river, something that flows: the Dnieper runs through Russia, Belarus and Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river, a thing that flows; the Dnieper is a major European river.

clue.text: Hesitates, for the reading is set in hell

indicators.note: is set in means the article and the letter are placed inside the word for hell

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, a name for hell
R stands for reading, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: Someone wavers because the scripture reading takes place in hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading' is one of the three Rs, and Dis is the Roman god of the underworld whose name stands for hell.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver indecisively is to hesitate; the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Understand girl gets made up

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: made up means the letters of gets are invented into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl understands she gets her make-up done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges GETS into GEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in and absorb information mentally is to comprehend it, a figurative sense of digestion.

clue.text: Toss cape through timidity

parts.note: to shy something is to fling or toss it
a ness is a headland or cape

explanation.surface: Throwing a cloak around out of bashfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a cloak but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashfulness or diffidence is timidity; the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Passionate about hostelry found down under

indicators.note: about means the passionate word goes around the hostelry word

parts.note: hot means passionate
a bar is a drinking place, a hostelry

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a pub they discovered in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Down under is Australia; the answer is the capital of Tasmania.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital of the Australian state of Tasmania, a place in the antipodes.

clue.text: Died in employment while celebrating

parts.note: OB is short for obiit, Latin for he or she died
someone serving is working for an employer

explanation.surface: Someone passed away on the job during the festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep or mark a festival or anniversary is to celebrate it, a sense of the verb observe.

clue.text: Play orchestral pieces in reverse order — that's splendid!

indicators.note: in reverse order means that fragment is read backwards
pieces means only a fragment of the words play orchestral is taken

explanation.surface: Perform the orchestral works backwards and it's magnificent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' takes LAYOR from 'Play orchestral'; 'in reverse order' turns it.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal or magnificent, fit for a king; royal treatment is splendid treatment.

clue.text: Guard decapitated candidate

indicators.note: decapitated means the head, the first letter, of the guard word is cut off

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A sentry has been beheaded in the line of duty; grim news for a candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something entered in a competition is a contender, a candidate for the prize.

clue.text: Instruments are found in containers

indicators.note: found in means the area unit letter is placed inside the containers

parts.note: tubs are containers
an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated A

explanation.surface: Musical instruments are kept in boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not a verb but the metric unit of land area, 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubas are large brass instruments, examples of musical instruments.

clue.text: Order a queen to skate

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen
the skate is a fish of the ray family

explanation.surface: Someone commands a queen to go skating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skate' looks like a verb but is the flat fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordered arrangement or line-up of things is an arrangement in order.

clue.text: Affected a bold pose in dance

indicators.note: something affected is put on or altered, so the letters of the phrase are reworked

explanation.surface: A dancer strikes a mannered, bold pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like an adjective for the pose but rearranges A BOLD POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish-style ballroom dance modelled on the bullfight; an example of a dance.

clue.text: Workman eats divine little fish

indicators.note: eats means the workman word swallows the divine letters inside it

parts.note: a tiler is a workman who lays tiles
DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a divine

explanation.surface: A labourer eats some heavenly small fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective but is a clergyman, DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a tiny fish such as a minnow or stickleback.

clue.text: A fabulous Greek nonet entertains

parts.note: the nine Muses of Greek myth, a nonet of fable

explanation.surface: A legendary Greek group of nine performers entertains.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert or delight someone is to entertain them; the third-person verbs are synonyms.
